record.title: Enumeration conjecture for nondegenerate hypermatrices avoiding a plane partition
record.statement:
In the format $2\times (k+1)\times k$, let $\Delta=\Delta_{1,(k-1)}$ and let $P=\langle\lambda,\mu\rangle$ be a plane partition with $P\subseteq\Delta$, where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are integer partitions of format $(k+1)\times k$. A hypermatrix **respects** $P$ when it satisfies the avoidance condition specified by the paper.

**Enumeration conjecture.** The number of nondegenerate $2\times (k+1)\times k$ hypermatrices over $\mathbb{F}_q$ which respect $P$ is

$$
q^{k^2}(q-1)^{2k}[k+1-\lambda_1]_q[k-\lambda_2]_q\cdots[2-\lambda_k]_q\cdot[k-\mu_1]_q[(k-1)-\mu_2]_q\cdots[1-\mu_k]_q.
$$

This conjecture gives the proposed enumeration of nondegenerate hypermatrices avoiding the plane partition $P$; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

record.title: The co-diameter-two co-chordal characterization conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a **co-chordal graph**, meaning that its complement is chordal, and suppose that the co-diameter of $G$, namely the diameter of its complement, is $2$. A graph is **non-trivially minimally tough** if it is minimally tough and not complete. For $\ell\geq 1$, let $S_{\ell,\ell,\ell}$ be obtained from three disjoint stars $K_{1,\ell}$ by adding a triangle between their centers.

**Co-diameter-two characterization conjecture.** The graph $G$ is non-trivially minimally tough if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $S_{\ell,\ell,\ell}$ for some $\ell\geq 1$.

This is the formal version of the preceding conjectural description of the unresolved co-diameter-$2$ case for co-chordal graphs, and remains open.

record.title: Szegö's construction conjecture for tight multigraphs
record.statement: Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a $(d,\ell)$-tight multigraph, with $\ell<\frac{4d+2}{3}$. Let $K_2^{2k-\ell}$ denote the graph with two vertices and $2k-\ell$ parallel edges, and let a $d$-dimensional $k$-extension be the graph operation used in the conjecture. **Szegö's conjecture.** The graph $\Gamma$ can be constructed from $K_2^{2k-\ell}$ using $d$-dimensional $k$-extensions, with no more than $2d-\ell$ parallel edges created between any pair of vertices. This conjecture strengthens the Frank–Szegö construction theorem by imposing the stated bound on parallel edges for $(d,\ell)$-tight multigraphs in the indicated range of $\ell$; its resolution is not specified in the source.

record.title: Reiher–Rödl–Schacht conjecture on uniform Turán density and vanishing orders
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a $k$-graph. For integers $1\leq\ell\leq k-3$, let $\pi_{\rm u}^{(\ell)}(F)$ denote its $\ell$-uniform Turán density. An **$(\ell+1)$-vanishing order** is an ordering of $V(F)$ admitting an $(\ell+1)$-vanishing coloring in the sense that every $(\ell+1)$-subset of positions in each edge receives its corresponding color. **Reiher–Rödl–Schacht conjecture.** For $1\leq\ell\leq k-3$,

$$
\pi_{\rm u}^{(\ell)}(F)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F\text{ has an }(\ell+1)\text{-vanishing order}.
$$

The conjecture connects zero uniform Turán density with the structural vanishing-order property; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

record.title: Conder's conjecture on simple groups with cosets of p-elements
record.statement: Let $S$ be a simple group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $S$. A group element is a **$p$-element** if its order is a power of $p$. **Conder's conjecture.** If a nontrivial coset $Pg$ consists entirely of $p$-elements, then $|P|=5$. The conjecture is motivated by the rarity of simple groups with this property and is supported by considerable evidence, but it remains open.
record.source_name: Ru Zhang and Rulin Shen, “On Zappa's question in the case of alternating groups”, arXiv:2603.09369 (2026).

record.title: The mixed-alphabet language conjecture for smooth words
record.statement:
Let $\mathpzc{A}=\{a,b\}$ be a mixed binary alphabet, let $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ be the set of infinite smooth words over $\mathpzc{A}$, let $\mathcal{C}_f^\infty$ be the set of finite f-smooth words, and let $\mathscr{L}(x)$ and $p_x(n)$ denote the factor language and factor complexity of $x$. **Mixed-alphabet language conjecture.** Over mixed alphabets, every smooth word $x$ satisfies

$$
\mathscr{L}(x)=\mathcal{C}_f^\infty,
$$

and, in particular,

$$
p_x(n)=p_{\mathcal{C}^\infty}(n)=p_{\mathcal{C}_f^\infty}(n).
$$

The conjecture is linked to recurrence and would imply complement and reversal invariance of every smooth-word language; the source contrasts it with failures over even and odd alphabets.

record.title: Higgins's perfect matching conjecture for bipartite tensor products
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a binary $n\times k$ matrix. Define $M\otimes M^T$ to be the symmetric $nk\times nk$ matrix indexed by pairs in $[n]\times[k]$, with entries

$$
(M\otimes M^T)((x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2))=M(x_1,y_2)M(x_2,y_1).
$$

A perfect matching is an involution on the vertex set such that every vertex is joined to its image by an edge. **Higgins's conjecture.** If the bipartite graph with both parts of size $nk$ and bipartite adjacency matrix $M\otimes M^T$ has a perfect matching, then the ordinary graph with adjacency matrix $M\otimes M^T$ also has a perfect matching. This question arises in the study of regular finite semigroups; it remains unproven in the general case, although the paper proves special cases and reduces it to a matrix inequality.

record.title: Weak balls conjecture for biregular bipartite multigraphs
record.statement: Let $M$ be a binary $n\times k$ matrix with non-negative integer entries, row sums $k$, and column sums $n$. Let $M\otimes M^T$ be the matrix associated with the corresponding tensor-product adjacency structure. **Weak balls conjecture.** The $(non\text{-}bipartite)$ $nk$-regular multigraph with $nk$ vertices and adjacency matrix $M\otimes M^T$ has a perfect matching. This conjecture is equivalent to Higgins's conjecture, and the paper proves special cases; the general case remains open.

record.title: Cluster factorization conjecture for outerplanar Landau diagrams
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{L}=G_u\cup H_u^{\triangle}$ be a planar Landau diagram, where $G$ is an outerplanar graph, and let $\Delta_{\mathcal{L}}$ denote its LS discriminant. **Cluster Factorization Conjecture.** The LS discriminant $\Delta_{\mathcal{L}}$ factors into a product of cluster variables. The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes the analogous factorization when $G$ is a tree; the conjecture proposes the extension to all outerplanar graphs and is unresolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The periodic efficient total girth coloring conjecture for cubic maps
record.statement: Let $M(G)$ be a connected simple cubic map of girth $4$ embedded in a genus-realizing orientable surface, and suppose all its belts have lengths $\ell$ with $\ell\equiv 0\pmod 4$. Let a DETGC and an RETGC denote the two types of efficient total girth colorings used in the source, let a 3PFC denote an associated 3-permutation face coloring, and let $G\square K_2$ be the prism graph. **Periodic efficient total girth coloring conjecture.** Such a map contains DETGCs and RETGCs with associated 3PFCs from which the original colorings can be recovered, yielding unique induced EGCs in $G\square K_2$. This is the paper's broad correspondence claim; the supplied text does not state a resolution.

record.title: Koszulity conjecture for Chow rings of flag or complete built matroids
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{M}$ be a matroid and let $\mathcal{G}$ be a building set such that $(\mathrm{M},\mathcal{G})$ is a flag or complete built matroid. **Koszulity conjecture.** The Chow ring of $(\mathrm{M},\mathcal{G})$ is Koszul.

This generalizes known Koszulity results for maximal building sets, augmented Chow rings, supersolvable built lattices, and the braid-matroid case with minimal building set. The source presents the general statement as open.

record.title: Non-empty core conjecture for correlated gift exchange coalitions
record.statement: Let $P$ be the set of players and let $\mathcal{K}$ be a coalition structure, with core stability meaning that no subset $S \subseteq P$ can deviate to form a new coalition and make all members of $S$ strictly better off. Assume standard gift exchange rules and correlated valuations. **Non-empty core conjecture.** The coalition formation game has a non-empty core. In particular, family-sized coalitions $K$ with $|K| \in \{2,3,4\}$ among players with correlated preferences are stable. The claim concerns the stability of coalition formation under correlated preferences; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or identify conditions beyond standard gift exchange rules.

record.title: Hersh–Reiner sharp stability conjecture for rank-selected homology of partition lattices
record.statement: Let $\Pi_n$ be the poset of set partitions of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ ordered by refinement, and let $S\subseteq\{1,2,\dots,n-2\}$. Write $\beta_S(\Pi_n)$ for the rank-selected homology $\mathfrak{S}_n$-representation associated with $S$. **Hersh–Reiner's sharp stability conjecture.** The representation $\beta_S(\Pi_n)$ stabilizes sharply at $4\max S-|S|+1$. The conjecture concerns the precise onset of representation stability for rank-selected homology of partition lattices; the supplied source does not indicate whether it has been resolved.

record.title: The global injectivity conjecture for projectivized coloring maps
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a cone of colorings, let $\mathcal M$ be the relevant moduli space, and let $A:\mathcal C\to\mathcal M$ be the associated locally affine map. Write $P\mathcal C$ and $P\mathcal M$ for their projectivizations, and let $PA:P\mathcal C\to P\mathcal M$ be the induced map. **Global injectivity conjecture.** The map

$$
PA:P\mathcal C\to P\mathcal M
$$

is globally injective.

This would strengthen the local injectivity supplied by the preceding theorem and, in particular, would make the projectivized parameterization globally faithful. The source presents it as a related conjecture after noting that the signature conjecture would imply only local injectivity; no resolution is given.

record.title: Dual defectivity and connectedness of the matroid
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a linear space with associated matroid $M(L)$, and let $L^{-1}$ be its reciprocal linear space. Write $
abla(L^{-1})$ for the dual variety of $L^{-1}$.

**Dual-defectivity conjecture.** The reciprocal linear space $L^{-1}$ is dual defective, meaning

$$
\dim \nabla(L^{-1})<n-1,
$$

if and only if the matroid $M(L)$ is not connected.

This conjecture characterizes dual defectivity in matroidal terms. It was first proposed by Clara Briand; if true, it identifies the connected flats as the relevant building-set components in the Newton-polytope description of the principal matroid determinant.

record.title: Wagner's conjecture on S- and I-Rayleigh regular matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a regular matroid. The properties S-Rayleigh and I-Rayleigh are the corresponding negative-dependence properties for matroids.

**Wagner's conjecture.** Every regular matroid is S- and I-Rayleigh.

Regular matroids include graphic and cographic matroids. A positive answer would confirm the conjectures of Kahn and of Grimmett and Winkler asserting that the unrooted spanning-forest distribution on a graph is negatively correlated; the conjecture's resolution is not specified in the source.

record.title: Weak immersion conjecture for Eulerian digraphs
record.statement:
Let an **Eulerian digraph** be a directed graph in which every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree, and let the **weak immersion** relation be the immersion relation in which branch vertices may be used internally by routed paths. Consider the class of all Eulerian digraphs.

**Weak immersion conjecture.** The class of Eulerian digraphs is well-quasi-ordered by weak immersion.

The source presents this as a fundamental contrast with strong immersion: its unbounded-degree antichain relies on forcing high-degree vertices to serve as branch vertices, whereas weak immersion permits them to route other paths. The conjecture remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: The N-regularity conjecture for mutable lattices
record.statement:
Let $L$ be a mutable lattice, and let $\operatorname{Hasse}(L)$ denote its Hasse diagram. Consider the underlying undirected graph of this diagram, and let $N$ be a constant.

**N-regularity conjecture.** Every vertex of the underlying undirected graph of $\operatorname{Hasse}(L)$ has degree $N$; equivalently, the graph is $N$-regular.

The paper states that the converse is false, so $N$-regularity does not characterize mutable lattices. The conjecture itself is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: Unimodality conjecture for the even part of reciprocal subsum numerators
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{num}(n,x)$ be the numerator polynomial associated with sums of reciprocals of subsum polynomials over partitions of $n$, and write 
$$
\mathrm{num}(n,x)=\mathrm{num}_0(n,x)+\mathrm{num}_1(n,x),
$$
 where $\mathrm{num}_0(n,x)$ is even and $\mathrm{num}_1(n,x)$ is odd. **Unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial $\mathrm{num}_0(n,x)$ is unimodal. The paper reports experimental evidence for this conjecture, which remains open.

record.title: Ternary-partition numerator conjecture at one
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal T(n)$ be the set of ternary partitions of $n$, meaning partitions whose parts are powers of $3$, and define 
$$
t(n)=\mathrm{num}_{\mathcal T}(n,1).
$$
 Let $\Delta$ denote the operator used in the source. **Ternary-partition recurrence conjecture.** One has $t(1)=t(2)=1$, 
$$
t(3n)=t(3n+1)=t(3n+2),
$$
 and 
$$
t(n)=\Delta\bigl(t(3n-2)/2^{2n}\bigr).
$$
 The statement is posed as an open question, but the supplied context does not define $\Delta$, so its precise meaning requires checking the paper.
